# Municipal Ordinance No. 05, Series of 2002

**Kautusang Bayan Blg. 05**

## Summary

Municipal Ordinance No. 05 (Kautusang Pambayan Blg. 05), Series of [[2002]], enacted by the [[Sangguniang Bayan]] of [[Municipality of Pitogo|Pitogo]], Quezon on August 19, 2002. This ordinance establishes requirements for obtaining Barangay Clearance and Police Clearance for any person seeking employment or residing within the municipality of Pitogo, Quezon. It mandates that all residents and job applicants must secure these clearance documents as a prerequisite for employment, business permits, and other municipal transactions.

## Key Provisions

- **Section 1** — Any person seeking employment or residence in the municipality of Pitogo, Quezon must secure a Barangay Clearance and Police Clearance, which shall serve as proof of good moral character and absence of any pending criminal or administrative case.
- **Section 2** — Any person who is a resident of Pitogo, Quezon and is applying for a business permit or any similar document for thirty (30) days must also secure a Barangay Clearance and Police Clearance together with any other requirements.
- **Section 3** — Applicants to the [[Sangguniang Bayan]] of Pitogo, Quezon who are non-residents or those whose background needs verification due to circumstances or involvement in any administrative institution or organization must also be required to present a Barangay Clearance or Police Clearance, and if warranted, the same shall be forwarded to the appropriate authority.
- **Section 4** — Fees: The processing fee for each clearance shall be Three Thousand Pesos (P2,000.00) for Barangay Clearance and the same for Police Clearance, with photocopying fee of Fifty Centavos (50 cents) per page, and shall not be lower than Four Hundred Twenty Pesos (P420) per person.
- **Section 5** — Enforcement shall be by the Kasunduang Pulidiya (Police) and Punong Barangay.
- **Section 6** — Penalties: Fines and other sanctions shall be imposed for violations.
- **Section 7** — This ordinance shall take effect ten (10) days after its publication.
